cards.text: Jesus is sitting on the Mount of Olives with four of His disciples: Peter, James, John and Andrew. They asked Him privately when the temple would be thrown down and what the sign would be. He's been warning them about false Christs and days of tribulation unseen since God made the world.
Now Jesus tells them what comes after that tribulation. And it starts WAY up in the sky.

cards.question: After that tribulation, what does Jesus say will happen to the sun?
With the sun darkened, Jesus says the moon will still give its light.

cards.text: Then Jesus gets to the stars. Friend, I bake under a night sky made for stars, so He has my FULL attention.

cards.question: Jesus says the stars will fall from the sky.
Jesus also names the powers of the heavens. What does He say will happen to them?

cards.text: Sun off, moon off, stars coming DOWN: that's darker than my old junk drawer, and I LIVED there. Then Jesus says what they will see.

cards.question: In all that dark, Jesus says they will see the prophet Elijah coming in the clouds.
The Son of Man is Jesus' name for Himself. How does Jesus say the Son of Man will come in the clouds?

answers.text: Hidden in a cloud of smoke

cards.text: Friend, it took ONE angel to get me out of ONE drawer. Here the Son of Man sends out the angels, plural.

cards.question: The Son of Man sends out the angels to ___ His elect.
Where do the angels gather the Son of Man's elect from?

cards.text: Then Jesus gives His disciples a lesson from a fig tree. Friend, I couldn't grow a fig tree if you taped the instructions to my hat, but even I can watch its branches.

cards.question: What do the fig tree's branches do that tells you a season is coming?

answers.text: They get tender and sprout leaves
They drop all of their fruit
They dry out and start to crack

cards.question: As soon as the fig branches sprout leaves, you know that ___ is near.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns the lesson from the tree to the things He's been telling them about.

cards.question: When the disciples see these things happening, what does Jesus say they should know?

answers.text: He is near right at the door
They still have plenty of time

cards.question: The fig tree lesson teaches the disciples to read the signs the way people read the seasons.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.”
Next He puts His words up against heaven and earth. Friend, that's the sky, the ground, and my whole little cookie planet too.

cards.question: Heaven and earth will pass away. What does Jesus say about His words?

cards.text: Things wear out, friend, just ask my old edges. Then Jesus talks about that day and hour, and whether anybody knows when it comes.

cards.question: Who does Jesus say knows about that day or hour?
Jesus says not even the Son knows that day or hour.
Since no one knows when the appointed time will come, what does Jesus tell His disciples to do?

answers.text: Be on guard and stay alert
Wait for a prophet to tell them

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a picture: a man going on a journey leaves his house. And he doesn't leave his servants with nothing to do.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture of the man going on a journey, what does the man put each servant in charge of?
The man also tells the servant at the door, the doorkeeper, to keep ___.

cards.text: Now the master of the house is coming back, but nobody knows when. It's like waiting on a delivery with no tracking: the SECOND you hop in the shower, the doorbell rings.

cards.question: Jesus names the times the master of the house might come back. Which stretch of the day do they cover?

cards.text: And here's the part that gets me. It's not just WHEN the master shows up. It's what he finds when he walks in.

cards.question: If the master arrives without notice, what does Jesus warn he might find?
Jesus ends His teaching on the Mount of Olives with a call to keep watch. He means it only for Peter, James, John and Andrew.

cards.text: What He says to them, He says to everyone: “Keep watch!” The snooze button has beaten stronger folks than me, friend, so in my bakery it's ovens warm, apron on, eyes OPEN.

findings.problem: Too many choices require prior knowledge or luck rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. In stop 1, the setups do not hint at what happens to the sun, moon or stars, how the Son of Man comes, or where the elect are gathered from. Later, stop 4 card 5 asks which stretch of day the four return times cover without ever naming those times, and stop 5 card 1 gives no setup for deciding whether the command is only for the four disciples. Discovery questions are not limited to a few, especially across stop 1.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The opening sentence retells the darkened sun and moon and the falling stars from Mark 13:24-25 before introducing verse 26, but the card cites only Mark 13:26. Its used range is Mark 13:24-26, unless the retelling is removed.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup says only that the Son of Man sends out angels; it gives no clue about their task. Choosing gather rather than judge or warn therefore depends on knowing the unseen BSB wording, not on reasoning out the meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
